argument:
The bull correctly compares $863.3m quarterly FCF with $461.766m net debt without promising a repayment timetable. This materially weakens financing-based objections and supports an operating-value thesis at 21.68x trailing earnings, rather than reliance only on 13.29x forecasts. Imperfect 68.16% conversion is compatible with substantial cash generation.

The remaining downside lies in concentrated advertising economics and extraordinary 77.68% operating margin: a change in platform economics could reduce earnings faster than the modest multiple suggests. Receivables of $2.171bn make collections relevant despite positive cash. The severe downtrend does not prove impairment, but cannot justify a bottom claim either. I accept that measured earnings and low net leverage make buying defensible; my argument against aggressive entry is durability and collection sensitivity, not a requirement for perfect conversion or invented misconduct.
key_points: Observed FCF materially exceeds net debt.
Trailing valuation supports a substantive operating case.
Margin and collections remain concentrated durability risks.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers financing fragility and cash absence decisively. The surviving bear case is narrower: exceptional margins and receivables can make apparently attractive earnings less durable, while the selloff alone proves neither impairment nor opportunity.
